sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes and Member Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bangalore in MVC No.3637/2020 dated 04.06.2022.

Court of Small Causes and Member Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bangalore

sentences.text:
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties.
3.
The appellant was respondent No.2 before the Tribunal and the respondents Nos.1 to 5 were the petitioners Nos.1 to 5 and respondent No.6 was respondent No.1.
Therefore, the rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the petitioners-claimants before the Tribunal is that they filed claim petition seeking compensation for the death of one Laxman Singh Rathore in the road traffic accident that occurred on 28.03.2020.

It is alleged that on 28.03.2020, the deceased was driving Maruti 800 car bearing NC: 2024:KHC:27817 No.KA-04-N-3932 along with his friends on Bangalore-Tumkur, NH-48 Road, Nelamangala Bypass Road towards Tumkur.
When they were proceeding in front of Madras-A-Fatima Masjid, the car was automatically got off.
All the inmates of the car got down and the car was taken towards extreme left side of the road.
The deceased was standing behind the car by putting the indicator and others were sitting on the side wall of the road.

At that time, a Tata Nexon car bearing No.TN-22-DR-2095 came on the same road from a direction in a high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased and parked car, due to which the deceased sustained multiple fatal injuries and succumbed to injuries.
Hence, the claimants being the wife, children and parents sought compensation.
5. The responding-insurance company filed statement of objection denying the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is further denied the accident, age and income of the deceased.
The owner of the vehicle also filed statement of objections and prayed for dismissing the petition.
The Tribunal framed three issues.
On behalf of the claimants, petitioner No.1 was examined was P.W.1 and one ore witness was examined as P.W.2 and got marked the documents as per exhibits P1 to 20.
On behalf of the respondents, no witnesses were examined and no documents were produced.

7. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.40,10,000/- along with 6% per annum from the rate of petition till realization, which is under challenge in this appeal.
8. The learned counsel for the appellant has contended that except producing two documents, there is no other document to show the income of the deceased that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal has committed error in taking Rs.20,000/- per month.

3 has also erred in granting the compensation of Rs.40,10,000/-.
Therefore, prayed for reducing the compensation.

The learned counsel for the respondents-petitioners has contended that the deceased was doing business and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has considered only Rs.20,000/-
per month, which is not an excessive amount.
Therefore, prayed for dismissing the appeal.
10. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.

11. The point that arise for consideration is :
(i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in taking Rs.20,000/- per month as income?
( ii) Whether the award calls for  interference.
12. On perusal of records, the claimants have stated that the deceased was doing the business and earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month.
Exhibits P.18 and P.19 are the passbooks of SBI bank of the deceased.
Based upon the said books, the Tribunal has considered Rs.20,000/- per month as income of the deceased.

It is pertinent to note that the sale takes place in the business, but the sale proceeds cannot be NC:
2024:KHC:27817 considered as income.
It is only sale and income to be deducted by cost wise, etc.
The claimants have not produced any documents to show that the deceased was filing IT returns and paying income tax.
Therefore, it cannot be considered that he was earning Rs.1,50,000/- per month in the business.
As per exhibits P.18 and P.19, it reveals that some transaction was made and the deceased received the amount and paid the amount.
Therefore, it cannot be said he was not an earning member and he was doing business and also some transaction took place as per exhibits P.18 and P.19.
Therefore, considering the same, I propose to consider Rs.16,000/- per month as income of the deceased, and 40% of the income towards future prospects which comes to Rs.22,400/-.
The claimants are more than 4 in number, hence, one-fourth of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased should be taken, which comes to Rs.16,800/- as net income.
Therefore, loss of dependency comes to Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.16,800/- x 15 x 12).
13. The compensation under all the other heads awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and the same is retained.
